title: Standards adapter
description: How to invoke exactly one (pack, version) and how to interpret what comes back. Every field is a fact discovered by reading that release; none may be inferred from a sibling. An adapter that cannot be fully constructed cannot be loaded, because a partially specified adapter would be an authority the orchestrator does not actually know how to interpret.

pack.description: Pack identity. Must appear in registry/packs.json.

version.description: The exact release this adapter was derived from. Never a range: supporting one release implies nothing about the next, and optimistic compatibility fails silently.

expectedCommit.description: The DEREFERENCED commit the tag must resolve to (refs/tags/<tag>^{}), not the tag-object SHA. Resolution compares against this. It is drift detection and a supply-chain control at once: CI runs exactly the commit that was reviewed, and a moved or force-pushed tag becomes a hard failure rather than silent execution of different code.

tagKind.description: Whether the release tag is annotated (a tag object that must be dereferenced with ^{}) or lightweight (a direct pointer to the commit). Recorded because the two produce different remote listings, and because a tag re-created in the other kind is a change to the released object that should fail rather than be absorbed.

entryPoint.description: Path to the executable script within the pack, relative to its root. Invoked directly rather than through the pack's npm scripts, which may hardcode their own targets.

verdictCommand.description: The subcommand that produces a verdict. Evidence-only subcommands are not verdicts and must never be used here.

argvTemplate.description: Argument vector with {{placeholders}}. Placeholders are substituted, never concatenated.

subcommandPosition.description: Whether the pack requires its subcommand as argv[0] or accepts it anywhere. Packs differ; assuming makes a silent mis-invocation.

requiresAbsolutePolicyPath.description: True where the pack's own policy discovery is unsafe and the orchestrator must pass and pre-verify an absolute path.

requiresAbsoluteTarget.description: True where omitting the target makes the pack fall back to its own fixtures.

output.description: The machine-readable output contract. A pack with no machine-readable output cannot be adapted; scraping human-readable text into a verdict is forbidden.

envelopeSchemaVersion.description: The schemaVersion this release emits from its verdict command. Recorded because at least one pack emits different values from different subcommands.

exitCodes.description: Every exit code this release is documented to produce. An undeclared code is an execution-contract failure, never a guess at the nearest declared one.

meaning.description: readVerdict: the envelope carries the conclusion. infrastructureFault: the pack could not evaluate, which is never the project's non-compliance. blocked: a prohibition fired.

verdictSource.description: Where the pack's own conclusion is read from. topLevelStatus: a named field. moduleDerived: the release has no single conclusion field and the interpreter module carries the derivation explicitly.

packVocabulary.description: The release's complete documented conclusion vocabulary. verdictMap must cover it exactly, so a vocabulary term added upstream cannot pass through unmapped.

verdictMap.description: Pack vocabulary to orchestrator outcome class. UNRESOLVED and CONFLICT are absent by design: they are orchestrator states, not conclusions any pack can reach about itself.

interpreter.description: Pack-specific code. Deliberately not a generic expression the orchestrator interprets: the recon proved 'meaningfully evaluated' has different semantics per pack, and a shared default would be exactly the cross-pack inference this architecture forbids.

module.description: Path relative to the registry directory. Must export readVerdict, positiveEvidence, describeEvidence, and readCoverage.

positiveEvidence.description: Human-readable statement of what the module's gate requires. Auditable without reading the code; the code remains the definition.

capabilities.description: Declared, never synthesized. An unsupported capability is reported as unsupported; the orchestrator does not emulate it.

knownHazards.description: Behaviours of this release that would produce a wrong reading if unmitigated. Each names its mitigation so the reason for an awkward invocation is not lost.

factSource.description: How the facts above were established. Every field is [FACT] and must be re-derived for a new release rather than carried forward.
